headline: Women's Career Gains Stall as Companies Pull Back Support

captions.x: Women's career gains are stalling as fewer US employers prioritise advancement. Ambition follows opportunity, the 11th Women in the Workplace study finds. https://themadamceo.com/article/fa2a0f3227.html

The 11th Women in the Workplace study finds fewer US employers prioritising women's advancement.

What backing have you had that made the biggest difference to your career?

captions.linkedin:
Fewer US employers are prioritising women's advancement, according to the 11th Women in the Workplace study.

If sponsorship and flexibility are quietly being cut, the support that moves women into management is getting thinner just as the first rung gets harder to reach.

The study also points to a first-ever ambition gap that closes when women get the same backing as men. The data suggests ambition follows opportunity, so a stalled career may reflect a lack of backing rather than a lack of drive.

What would change in your organisation if sponsorship were treated as a core part of talent management?

Maternity leave rankings are having a moment. A new Business Insider roundup of 18 major US employers is the latest addition to a crowded field, and the details behind each ranking matter more than the headline number.

Leave policy shapes whether you can step into a senior role without losing ground, both financially and in your career trajectory.

A strong, clearly written policy also signals how a company treats working parents. Weigh it as seriously as pay and title when you assess an offer or a promotion.
